sanskrit: gatān ṛṣīṃs tathā devān asurāṃś ca tathā gatān lokād asmāt paraṃ lokaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who beholds how the sages have passed away, and the gods likewise, and the asuras too departed, gone from this world to the world beyond — he is released.

sanskrit: prabhāvair anvitās tais taiḥ pārthivendrāḥ sahasraśaḥ ye gatāḥ pṛthivīṃ tyaktvā iti jñātvā vimucyate
english: Knowing that kings of the earth by the thousand, endowed with this power and that, have departed, abandoning the earth — by this knowledge he is set free.

sanskrit: arthāṃś ca durlabhāṃl loke kleśāṃś ca sulabhāṃs tathā duḥkhaṃ caiva kuṭumbārthe yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who sees how hard wealth is to win in this world, how easily afflictions come, and the suffering borne for the sake of family — he is released.

sanskrit: apatyānāṃ ca vaiguṇyaṃ janaṃ viguṇam eva ca paśyan bhūyiṣṭhaśo loke ko mokṣaṃ nābhipūjayet
english: Seeing so widely in the world the worthlessness of offspring and the unworthiness of people, who would not hold liberation in highest honour?

sanskrit: śāstrāl lokāc ca yo buddhaḥ sarvaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ asāram iva mānuṣyaṃ sarvathā mukta eva saḥ
english: The man who, awakened by scripture and by the world, sees the whole of human existence as without substance — he is in every way already free.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mama vaco bhavāṃś caratu muktavat gārhasthye yadi te mokṣe kṛtā buddhir aviklavā
english: Having heard this counsel of mine, let your honour wander as one already liberated, even in the householder's life, if your mind is fixed unwavering upon release.

sanskrit: tat tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā samyak sa pṛthivīpatiḥ mokṣajaiś ca guṇair yuktaḥ pālayām āsa ca prajāḥ
english: Having rightly heard that counsel of his, the lord of the earth, endowed with the virtues born of liberation, governed his subjects.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tiṣṭhate me sadā tāta kautūhalam idaṃ hṛdi tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi tvattaḥ kurupitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A certain curiosity ever abides in my heart, dear sire; this I wish to hear from you, O grandsire of the Kurus.

sanskrit: kathaṃ devarṣir uśanā sadā kāvyo mahāmatiḥ asurāṇāṃ priyakaraḥ surāṇām apriye rataḥ
english: How was it that the divine seer Uśanas, son of Kavi, ever of great wisdom, did good to the asuras and delighted in what was unwelcome to the gods?

sanskrit: vardhayām āsa tejaś ca kimartham amitaujasām nityaṃ vairanibaddhāś ca dānavāḥ surasattamaiḥ
english: For what purpose did he augment the might of those of measureless force, the dānavas, who were ever bound in enmity with the best of the gods?

sanskrit: kathaṃ cāpy uśanā prāpa śukratvam amaradyutiḥ ṛddhiṃ ca sa kathaṃ prāptaḥ sarvam etad bravīhi me
english: And how did Uśanas, radiant as the immortals, attain to the state of Śukra, and how did he gain his prosperity? Tell me all of this.

sanskrit: na yāti ca sa tejasvī madhyena nabhasaḥ katham etad icchāmi vijñātuṃ nikhilena pitāmaha
english: And how is it that the luminous one does not pass through the middle of the sky? This I wish to understand in full, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahitaḥ sarvam etad yathātatham yathāmati yathā caitac chrutapūrvaṃ mayānagha
english: Bhīṣma said: Listen attentively, O king, to all of this as it truly is, according to my understanding and as I have heard it before, O sinless one.

sanskrit: eṣa bhārgavadāyādo muniḥ satyo dṛḍhavrataḥ asurāṇāṃ priyakaro nimitte karuṇātmake
english: This sage, heir of Bhṛgu, truthful and firm in his vows, did good to the asuras out of a compassionate cause.

sanskrit: indro 'tha dhanado rājā yakṣarakṣodhipaḥ sa ca prabhaviṣṇuś ca kośasya jagataś ca tathā prabhuḥ
english: Now Indra, and King Kubera the giver of wealth, lord of the yakṣas and rākṣasas — he too was master of the treasury and lord of the world.

sanskrit: tasyātmānam athāviśya yogasiddho mahāmuniḥ ruddhvā dhanapatiṃ devaṃ yogena hṛtavān vasu
english: The great sage, perfected in yoga, then entering into himself and confining the god Kubera, lord of wealth, by his yoga carried off his riches.

sanskrit: hṛte dhane tataḥ śarma na lebhe dhanadas tathā āpannamanyuḥ saṃvignaḥ so 'bhyagāt surasattamam
english: His wealth thus stolen, Kubera could find no peace; seized with wrath and agitated, he went to the best of the gods.

sanskrit: nivedayām āsa tadā śivāyāmitatejase devaśreṣṭhāya rudrāya saumyāya bahurūpiṇe
english: He then made his plaint to Śiva of measureless splendour, to Rudra, foremost of gods, the gracious one of many forms.

sanskrit: kubera uvāca yogātmakenośanasā ruddhvā mama hṛtaṃ vasu yogenātmagatiṃ kṛtvā niḥsṛtaś ca mahātapāḥ
english: Kubera said: By Uśanas, master of yoga, my wealth has been confined and carried off; the great ascetic, having made his course by yoga, has departed.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etac chrutvā tataḥ kruddho mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ saṃraktanayano rājañ śūlam ādāya tasthivān
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing this, the great yogin Maheśvara grew wroth; his eyes flushed red, O king, he took up his trident and stood ready.

sanskrit: kvāsvau kvāsāv iti prāha gṛhītvā paramāyudham uśanā dūratas tasya babhau jñātvā cikīrṣitam
english: "Where is he, where is he?" he cried, grasping his supreme weapon; but Uśanas, knowing his intent, shone forth at a distance from him.

sanskrit: sa mahāyogino buddhvā taṃ roṣaṃ vai mahātmanaḥ gatim āgamanaṃ vetti sthānaṃ vetti tataḥ prabhuḥ
english: Perceiving the wrath of the great-souled, mighty yogin, the lord then knew his going and his coming, and knew his place.

sanskrit: saṃcintyogreṇa tapasā mahātmānaṃ maheśvaram uśanā yogasiddhātmā śūlāgre pratyadṛśyata
english: Having meditated by his fierce austerity upon the great-souled Maheśvara, Uśanas, his self perfected in yoga, appeared upon the point of the trident.

sanskrit: vijñātarūpaḥ sa tadā tapaḥsiddhena dhanvinā jñātvā śūlaṃ ca deveśaḥ pāṇinā samanāmayat
english: His form thus recognized by the bow-bearer perfected in austerity, the lord of gods, perceiving him, bent down the trident with his hand.

sanskrit: ānatenātha śūlena pāṇināmitatejasā pinākam iti covāca śūlam ugrāyudhaḥ prabhuḥ
english: With the trident now bent down by his hand of measureless might, the lord of the terrible weapon named that trident "Pināka."

sanskrit: pāṇimadhyagataṃ dṛṣṭvā bhārgavaṃ tam umāpatiḥ āsyaṃ vivṛtya kakudī pāṇiṃ saṃprākṣipac chanaiḥ
english: Seeing the descendant of Bhṛgu come into the midst of his hand, the lord of Umā, the bull-marked one, opened his mouth and slowly cast his hand toward it.

sanskrit: sa tu praviṣṭa uśanā koṣṭhaṃ māheśvaraṃ prabhuḥ vyacarac cāpi tatrāsau mahātmā bhṛgunandanaḥ
english: But the lord Uśanas, that great-souled delight of Bhṛgu, having entered into the belly of Maheśvara, wandered about within.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kimarthaṃ vyacarad rājann uśanā tasya dhīmataḥ jaṭhare devadevasya kiṃ cākārṣīn mahādyutiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For what reason, O king, did Uśanas wander in the belly of that wise god of gods, and what did the greatly radiant one do there?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca purā so 'ntarjalagataḥ sthāṇubhūto mahāvrataḥ varṣāṇām abhavad rājan prayutāny arbudāni ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Long ago, O king, that great keeper of vows abode beneath the waters, motionless as a post, for millions and tens of millions of years.

sanskrit: udatiṣṭhat tapas taptvā duścaraṃ sa mahāhradāt tato devātidevas taṃ brahmā samupasarpata
english: Having performed austerity hard to endure, he rose up from the great lake; then Brahmā, god beyond the gods, drew near to him.

sanskrit: tapovṛddhim apṛcchac ca kuśalaṃ cainam avyayam tapaḥ sucīrṇam iti ca provāca vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
english: He asked after the growth of his austerity and after his unfailing welfare; and the bull-bannered one said, "Well practised is your austerity."

sanskrit: tatsaṃyogena vṛddhiṃ cāpy apaśyat sa tu śaṃkaraḥ mahāmatir acintyātmā satyadharmarataḥ sadā
english: And by that union Śaṃkara perceived his increase — he of great wisdom, of inconceivable nature, ever devoted to truth and dharma.

sanskrit: sa tenāḍhyo mahāyogī tapasā ca dhanena ca vyarājata mahārāja triṣu lokeṣu vīryavān
english: Enriched thereby in austerity and in wealth, that great yogin, valorous, shone forth throughout the three worlds, O great king.

sanskrit: tataḥ pinākī yogātmā dhyānayogaṃ samāviśat uśanā tu samudvigno nililye jaṭhare tataḥ
english: Then the Pināka-bearer, his self given to yoga, entered into the yoga of meditation; but Uśanas, alarmed, concealed himself within the belly.

sanskrit: tuṣṭāva ca mahāyogī devaṃ tatrastha eva ca niḥsāraṃ kāṅkṣamāṇas tu tejasā pratyahanyata
english: And the great yogin, dwelling there, praised the god; but, seeking a way out, he was thrust back by his splendour.

sanskrit: uśanā tu tadovāca jaṭharastho mahāmuniḥ prasādaṃ me kuruṣveti punaḥ punar ariṃdama
english: Then Uśanas, the great sage, dwelling in the belly, spoke: "Show me your grace," again and again, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahādevo gaccha śiśnena mokṣaṇam iti srotāṃsi sarvāṇi ruddhvā tridaśapuṃgavaḥ
english: Mahādeva said to him, "Go forth; your release shall be by the member" — for the bull of the gods had stopped up all the other openings.

sanskrit: apaśyamānaḥ sa dvāraṃ sarvataḥpihito muniḥ paryakrāmad dahyamāna itaś cetaś ca tejasā
english: Finding no door, shut in on every side, the sage wandered to and fro, burning in that splendour.

sanskrit: sa viniṣkramya śiśnena śukratvam abhipedivān kāryeṇa tena nabhaso nāgacchata ca madhyataḥ
english: Coming forth by the member, he attained the state of Śukra; and by that very deed he comes not through the middle of the sky.

sanskrit: niṣkrāntam atha taṃ dṛṣṭvā jvalantam iva tejasā bhavo roṣasamāviṣṭaḥ śūlodyatakaraḥ sthitaḥ
english: Then, seeing him come forth blazing as it were with splendour, Bhava, filled with wrath, stood with his trident raised in his hand.

sanskrit: nyavārayata taṃ devī kruddhaṃ paśupatiṃ patim putratvam agamad devyā vārite śaṃkare ca saḥ
english: But the goddess restrained her wrathful lord, the master of beasts; and when Śaṃkara was thus stayed by the goddess, the sage came to the state of her son.

sanskrit: devy uvāca hiṃsanīyas tvayā naiṣa mama putratvam āgataḥ na hi devodarāt kaś cin niḥsṛto nāśam archati
english: The goddess said: This one is not to be slain by you, for he has come to be my son; and none who has issued from a god's womb meets with destruction.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ prīto 'bhavad devyāḥ prahasaṃś cedam abravīt gacchatv eṣa yathākāmam iti rājan punaḥ punaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then he was pleased with the goddess, and laughing said this: "Let him go as he wills," O king, again and again.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇamya varadaṃ devaṃ devīm umāṃ tathā uśanā prāpa tad dhīmān gatim iṣṭāṃ mahāmuniḥ
english: Then, bowing to the boon-granting god and to the goddess Umā, the wise Uśanas, the great sage, attained the course he desired.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ tāta bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ caritaṃ bharataśreṣṭha yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: This deed of the great-souled descendant of Bhṛgu I have related to you, dear son, O best of the Bhāratas, as you have asked of me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ataḥ paraṃ mahābāho yac chreyas tad vadasva me na tṛpyāmy amṛtasyeva vacasas te pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Beyond this, O mighty-armed one, tell me what is best; I am not sated with your words, as if with nectar, O grandsire.

sanskrit: kiṃ karma puruṣaḥ kṛtvā śubhaṃ puruṣasattama śreyaḥ param avāpnoti pretya ceha ca tad vada
english: By doing what auspicious deed, O best of men, does a man attain the supreme good both hereafter and here? Tell me that.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi yathā pūrvaṃ mahāyaśāḥ parāśaraṃ mahātmānaṃ papraccha janako nṛpaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you how, in former times, King Janaka of great fame questioned the great-souled Parāśara.

sanskrit: kiṃ śreyaḥ sarvabhūtānām asmiṃl loke paratra ca yad bhavet pratipattavyaṃ tad bhavān prabravītu me
english: What is the highest good of all beings in this world and the next, and what ought to be attained — that may your honour declare to me.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tapasā yuktaḥ sarvadharmavidhānavit nṛpāyānugrahamanā munir vākyam athābravīt
english: Then that sage, endowed with austerity and knowing the whole ordinance of dharma, his mind set on favouring the king, spoke these words.

sanskrit: dharma eva kṛtaḥ śreyān iha loke paratra ca tasmād dhi paramaṃ nāsti yathā prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Dharma alone, when practised, is the better thing both in this world and the next; for there is nothing higher than it, as the wise have declared.

sanskrit: pratipadya naro dharmaṃ svargaloke mahīyate dharmātmakaḥ karmavidhir dehināṃ nṛpasattama tasminn āśramiṇaḥ santaḥ svakarmāṇīha kurvate
english: Embracing dharma, a man is exalted in the world of heaven; the ordinance of action is itself of the nature of dharma for embodied beings, O best of kings, and within it the good who keep the stations of life perform their proper duties here.

sanskrit: caturvidhā hi lokasya yātrā tāta vidhīyate martyā yatrāvatiṣṭhante sā ca kāmāt pravartate
english: For the world's course is ordained of four kinds, dear son, in which mortals abide; and it proceeds from desire.

sanskrit: sukṛtāsukṛtaṃ karma niṣevya vividhaiḥ kramaiḥ daśārdhapravibhaktānāṃ bhūtānāṃ bahudhā gatiḥ
english: Having performed deeds well-done and ill-done by manifold gradations, manifold is the course of beings, who are divided according to the five elements.

sanskrit: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi yathā bhāṇḍaṃ niṣicyate tathā niṣicyate jantuḥ pūrvakarmavaśānugaḥ
english: Just as a vessel of gold or of silver is cast in its mould, so is a creature cast, subject to the power of its former deeds.

sanskrit: nābījāj jāyate kiṃ cin nākṛtvā sukham edhate sukṛtī vindati sukhaṃ prāpya dehakṣayaṃ naraḥ
english: Nothing arises from no seed, nor does one prosper in happiness without acting; the doer of good deeds, having attained the dissolution of the body, finds happiness.

sanskrit: daivaṃ tāta na paśyāmi nāsti daivasya sādhanam svabhāvato hi saṃsiddhā devagandharvadānavāḥ
english: Fate I do not perceive, dear son; there is no means of accomplishing fate; for gods, gandharvas, and dānavas are perfected by their own nature.

sanskrit: pretya jātikṛtaṃ karma na smaranti sadā janāḥ te vai tasya phalaprāptau karma cāpi caturvidham
english: After death, people do not always remember the deeds done in their birth; yet they reap the fruit of that deed, and the deed too is fourfold.

sanskrit: lokayātrāśrayaś caiva śabdo vedāśrayaḥ kṛtaḥ śāntyarthaṃ manasas tāta naitad vṛddhānuśāsanam
english: The word resting on the conduct of the world and resting on the Veda was made for the sake of the mind's peace, dear son; this is not the teaching of the elders.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā manasā vācā karmaṇā ca caturvidham kurute yādṛśaṃ karma tādṛśaṃ pratipadyate
english: By eye, by mind, by speech, and by action — fourfold; whatever kind of deed a man does, that very kind does he obtain.

sanskrit: nirantaraṃ ca miśraṃ ca phalate karma pārthiva kalyāṇaṃ yadi vā pāpaṃ na tu nāśo 'sya vidyate
english: Unceasingly, and in mixed measure, does action bear fruit, O king, whether it be good or evil; but there is no destruction of it.

sanskrit: kadā cit sukṛtaṃ tāta kūṭastham iva tiṣṭhati majjamānasya saṃsāre yāvad duḥkhād vimucyate
english: Sometimes, dear son, a good deed stands as though unmoved at the summit, for one sinking in the round of existence, until he is freed from sorrow.

sanskrit: tato duḥkhakṣayaṃ kṛtvā sukṛtaṃ karma sevate sukṛtakṣayād duṣkṛtaṃ ca tad viddhi manujādhipa
english: Then, having worn away his sorrow, he enjoys his good deed; and from the exhaustion of the good deed comes the ill-done one — know this, O lord of men.

sanskrit: damaḥ kṣamā dhṛtis tejaḥ saṃtoṣaḥ satyavāditā hrīr ahiṃsāvyasanitā dākṣyaṃ ceti sukhāvahāḥ
english: Self-restraint, forbearance, firmness, vigour, contentment, truthful speech, modesty, freedom from cruelty and from vice, and skill — these bring happiness.

sanskrit: duṣkṛte sukṛte vāpi na jantur ayato bhavet nityaṃ manaḥsamādhāne prayateta vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: Whether in ill-doing or in good-doing, let a creature not be unrestrained; the discerning man should ever strive for the composure of the mind.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ parasya sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vāpi sevate karoti yādṛśaṃ karma tādṛśaṃ pratipadyate
english: This man does not partake of another's good deed or ill deed; whatever kind of deed he does, that very kind does he obtain.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe samādhāya pumān anyena gacchati anyenaiva janaḥ sarvaḥ saṃgato yaś ca pārthiva
english: Having laid by his pleasure and pain, a man departs alone; and by another path goes every man, even he with whom one has been joined, O king.

sanskrit: pareṣāṃ yad asūyeta na tat kuryāt svayaṃ naraḥ yo hy asūyus tathāyuktaḥ so 'vahāsaṃ niyacchati
english: What a man would resent in others, that let him not do himself; for he who is envious and so disposed brings mockery upon himself.

sanskrit: bhīrū rājanyo brāhmaṇaḥ sarvabhakṣo; vaiśyo 'nīhāvān hīnavarṇo 'lasaś ca vidvāṃś cāśīlo vṛttahīnaḥ kulīnaḥ; satyād bhraṣṭo brāhmaṇaḥ strī ca duṣṭā
english: A cowardly kṣatriya, a brāhmaṇa who eats all things, an idle vaiśya, a man of low birth who is slothful, a learned man of bad character, a man of good lineage destitute of conduct, a brāhmaṇa fallen from truth, and a wicked woman —

sanskrit: rāgī muktaḥ pacamāno ''tmahetor; mūrkho vaktā nṛpahīnaṃ ca rāṣṭram ete sarve śocyatāṃ yānti rājan; yaś cāyuktaḥ snehahīnaḥ prajāsu
english: a passionate ascetic who has renounced, one who cooks for his own sake, a fool who would teach, and a realm without a king — all these come to a pitiable state, O king, and so too the ruler who is heedless and devoid of affection toward his subjects.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca manoratharathaṃ prāpya indriyārthahayaṃ naraḥ raśmibhir jñānasaṃbhūtair yo gacchati sa buddhimān
english: Parāśara said: The man who, having gained the chariot of his desires drawn by the horses of the sense-objects, drives it with the reins born of knowledge — he is wise.

sanskrit: sevāśritena manasā vṛttihīnasya śasyate dvijātihastān nirvṛttā na tu tulyāt parasparam
english: For one bereft of livelihood, a mind given to service is commended; sustenance is praised when it comes from the hand of the twice-born, but not from an equal in mutual exchange.

sanskrit: āyur nasulabhaṃ labdhvā nāvakarṣed viśāṃ pate utkarṣārthaṃ prayatate naraḥ puṇyena karmaṇā
english: Having gained a life-span not easily won, a man should not drag himself down, O lord of peoples; rather let him strive for his elevation by meritorious action.

sanskrit: varṇebhyo 'pi paribhraṣṭaḥ sa vai saṃmānam arhati na tu yaḥ satkriyāṃ prāpya rājasaṃ karma sevate
english: Even one fallen away from the classes deserves honour, but not he who, having attained right conduct, then practises deeds of passion.

sanskrit: varṇotkarṣam avāpnoti naraḥ puṇyena karmaṇā durlabhaṃ tam alabdhā hi hanyāt pāpena karmaṇā
english: A man attains elevation of class by meritorious action; but not having gained that hard-won state, he would destroy it by sinful action.

sanskrit: ajñānād dhi kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tapasaivābhinirṇudet pāpaṃ hi karma phalati pāpam eva svayaṃ kṛtam tasmāt pāpaṃ na seveta karma duḥkhaphalodayam
english: Sin done out of ignorance one may dispel by austerity alone; for a sinful deed bears sinful fruit, the very sin one has done oneself; therefore let none practise sin, the deed whose fruit is the rising of sorrow.

sanskrit: pāpānubandhaṃ yat karma yady api syān mahāphalam na tat seveta medhāvī śuciḥ kusalilaṃ yathā
english: A deed bound up with sin, though it should be of great fruit, the wise and pure man would not practise — even as he would shun foul water.

sanskrit: kiṃkaṣṭam anupaśyāmi phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ pratyāpannasya hi sato nātmā tāvad virocate
english: What greater misery do I behold than the fruit of a sinful deed? For even of one who has turned back and become good, the self does not yet shine forth.

sanskrit: pratyāpattiś ca yasyeha bāliśasya na jāyate tasyāpi sumahāṃs tāpaḥ prasthitasyopajāyate
english: And for the fool in whom no turning-back arises here, exceedingly great is the anguish that comes upon him as he sets forth on his way.

sanskrit: viraktaṃ śodhyate vastraṃ na tu kṛṣṇopasaṃhitam prayatnena manuṣyendra pāpam evaṃ nibodha me
english: A garment whose dye has faded can be cleansed, but not one steeped in black, for all one's effort; understand sin thus from me, O lord of men.
